hero.headline: JetBlue ending Vero Beach to New York JFK route in September due to low demand
hero.teaser: JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as th
hero.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating in September. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates based on passenger numbers. "It's just the way that that market works, and air carriers will fluctuate based off of demand," Dambeck said. He added that JetBlue "just wasn't seeing what they were hoping for" with the New York route.

Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot at success. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time if given more opportunity. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. He noted the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach, saying, "It's easy. It's close." His comments reflect concerns from local travelers who appreciated having direct access to New York without driving to larger airports in South Florida or Orlando.

The Boston route continues to perform well at Vero Beach Regional Airport, with Dambeck saying "Boston is seeing great demand." Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time, demonstrating continued interest in that northeastern connection. The contrast between the two routes highlights how different markets can perform differently even when serving similar geographic regions. While both Boston and New York are major northeastern cities, the Boston service has attracted enough passengers to remain viable while the JFK route struggled to build a sustainable customer base.

Dambeck said the door is not closed on the JFK route returning in the future, noting "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back." This leaves open the possibility that JetBlue could restore service to New York if conditions change or demand increases. Airlines regularly reassess their route networks based on seasonal patterns, economic conditions, and shifting travel preferences. For now, Vero Beach travelers seeking to reach New York will need to connect through other cities or use alternative airports.

cards.headline: Two men killed in early morning shooting on Southeast Rivergreen Circle in Port St. Lucie
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie Police Department is investigating a double fatal shooting that occurred early Sunday morning in a residential neighborhood. Officers responded around 3:30 a.m. to the 1300 block of Southeast Rivergreen Circle after receiving multiple 911 calls reporting gunshots. When officers arrived, they found two adult men suffering from multiple gunshot wounds in the driveways of a residence. Both victims were taken to separate local hospitals, where they later died from their injuries.

Police identified the victims as Carl Loubeau, 24, and Juliun Stokes, 22. Preliminary investigators believe some of the people involved had been socializing earlier in the evening before returning to a home on Southeast Rivergreen Circle. Police said a verbal altercation occurred outside the residence over a residential key and escalated into an exchange of gunfire between two of the individuals involved.

Neighbor John Adams was awake working on his bicycle in his garage when he heard the gunfire. "I was just working on my bicycle and I heard gunshots. Maybe two, three and I stayed in the garage and then I heard a girl screaming," Adams said. He described the emergency response as overwhelming. "Every police officer in Port St. Lucie was here, there was twenty squads, two ambulances, two firetrucks, a helicopter. It was just mayhem," Adams said. A police officer told Adams they took a picture of 16 casings at the scene. Adams expressed his sorrow over the incident, saying his heart goes out to the victims. Another neighbor who did not want to be identified told reporters she dialed 911 and stayed with one of the wounded men until help arrived.

Investigators believe the shooting was an isolated incident involving people who knew one another and said there is no ongoing threat to the public. All parties involved have either been detained or are cooperating with investigators, according to police. The investigation remains active as detectives continue conducting interviews, processing evidence and reviewing available information. Police said additional details, including any potential criminal charges, will be released as the investigation progresses. Anyone with information who has not yet spoken with detectives is asked to contact the Port St. Lucie Police Department.

cards.headline: Snyder Drives in Five as St. Lucie Mets Hold Off Cardinals, 8-6
cards.teaser:
Trey Snyder delivered a career day at the plate Sunday as the St. Lucie Mets held off a late Palm Beach Cardinals rally for an 8-6 victory at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

Snyder
cards.body:
Trey Snyder delivered a career day at the plate Sunday as the St. Lucie Mets held off a late Palm Beach Cardinals rally for an 8-6 victory at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

Snyder went 4-for-5 with a home run, triple and five RBIs, helping St. Lucie win the three-game series two games to one.

After allowing the Cardinals to score first in each of the opening two games, the Mets took control with three runs in the first inning.

Randy Guzman opened the scoring with a 107 mph ground ball that Palm Beach third baseman Jonathan Mejia stopped but could not make a throw on, allowing Marco Vargas to score. Snyder followed with a two-run single that gave the Mets a 3-0 lead.

Starting pitcher Ethan Lanthier worked through early traffic and completed 2 1/3 scoreless innings. He allowed one hit and struck out four.

Tyler McLoughlin followed with 1 2/3 scoreless innings and earned the victory, improving his record to 2-2. McLoughlin has allowed only one earned run over his last 12 appearances and has now recorded six consecutive scoreless outings.

St. Lucie added three more runs in the third inning when Snyder launched his second home run of the season. The three-run shot brought home Mike Tauchman and Guzman and extended the Mets' advantage to 6-0.

Snyder continued his strong afternoon with a triple in the seventh inning. Branny De Oleo then hit his seventh home run of the season, a two-run shot that pushed St. Lucie's lead to 8-1.

Palm Beach made the game interesting in the bottom of the seventh.

Yairo Padilla hit his first home run of the season, a grand slam against Ernesto Mercedes, as the Cardinals scored five runs in the inning and cut the Mets' lead to 8-6.

Palm Beach brought the potential tying run to the plate in the ninth after Trevor Haskins was hit by a pitch. Miguel Mejias responded by striking out the next three batters to finish the game and earn his third save of the season.

St. Lucie pitchers combined for 17 strikeouts, marking the third consecutive game in which the Mets recorded double-digit strikeouts.

The Mets improved to 8-14 in the second half and 41-47 overall. Palm Beach fell to 13-10 in the second half and 65-43 overall.

St. Lucie will have an off day Monday before opening a new series against the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels on Tuesday. First pitch is scheduled for 6:05 p.m.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie neighbors express concerns over commercial rezoning near Tradition
cards.teaser: Joseph and Margaret Mucciolo live along the edge of a nearly 9.5-acre property near Crosstown Parkway and SW Fairgreen Drive that is scheduled for a second reading and final vote before city council Monday.
cards.body:
Joseph and Margaret Mucciolo live along the edge of a nearly 9.5-acre property near Crosstown Parkway and SW Fairgreen Drive in Tradition that could soon be transformed from residential land to commercial use. The Port St. Lucie City Council is scheduled to hold a second reading and final vote Monday on a rezoning request that has prompted concerns from neighboring residents about overdevelopment and quality of life impacts.

The request, submitted by Winding River Crosstown, LLC, would amend the Tradition Master Planned Unit Development plan by removing the property from a residential designation and creating a new parcel designated for retail and office uses. According to the city, the change would allow for future commercial development on the site, though any future project would still need to go through additional review and approval processes. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval of the amendment with conditions in May.

Those conditions include a 10-foot enhanced landscape buffer and architectural wall along portions of the property bordering residential areas, requirements to limit lighting impacts, and eliminating a possible future connection to SW Glenbrook Drive. However, Joseph Mucciolo expressed concerns about the proposed wall, saying if they put up a wall it's going to look like a prison. The couple worries that losing the open space behind their home could fundamentally alter the neighborhood character they chose when moving to the area.

Margaret Mucciolo said they do not want over development. The family's concerns reflect broader anxieties about balancing growth with maintaining the residential quality that drew people to Tradition in the first place. Joseph Mucciolo indicated the changes could be significant enough to drive them away from their home, saying if these things come to pass, they may seek other grounds and other places to go. The rezoning proposal represents one of many land use debates facing Port St. Lucie as the city continues to grow and developers seek to convert properties to more intensive commercial uses near established residential neighborhoods.

cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets fell behind early and could not complete a late comeback in a 7-4 loss to the Palm Beach Cardinals on Saturday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

The loss evened
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets fell behind early and could not complete a late comeback in a 7-4 loss to the Palm Beach Cardinals on Saturday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. The loss evened the three-game series at one game apiece and set up a rubber match Sunday afternoon. Palm Beach opened the scoring with three runs in the bottom of the first inning when Brayden Smith singled to center field and an error by D'Andre Smith allowed the Cardinals to capitalize. Ryan Weingartner and Sebastian Dos Santos scored on the play before Brayden Smith came around to give Palm Beach a 3-0 advantage. St. Lucie responded with two runs in the second inning as Chase Meggers delivered an RBI single with runners on the corners, scoring AJ Salgado. Jeremy Rodriguez then brought Simon Juan home on a fielder's choice to cut the Cardinals' lead to 3-2.

Palm Beach began pulling away in the fourth inning when Alex Birg drove in Yordalin Pena with an RBI single before Dos Santos launched a two-run home run. The Cardinals eventually built a 7-2 lead. Antonio Jimenez gave the Mets another run in the top of the sixth inning with a solo home run, his sixth of the season and fourth during July, cutting the Palm Beach lead to 7-3. The Mets mounted one final rally in the ninth inning and brought the potential tying run to the plate, but Palm Beach reliever Nathan Shinn escaped the threat and secured the victory for the Cardinals.

The Mets bullpen settled the game down after Joe Scarborough entered from the bullpen. Scarborough delivered two scoreless and hitless innings while striking out four batters, marking his second consecutive scoreless appearance at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. Caden Wooster followed Scarborough with another strong relief appearance, allowing just one hit over two scoreless innings and striking out four. Scarborough and Wooster combined to strike out eight batters over four shutout innings. St. Lucie's pitching staff finished the game with 12 strikeouts, reaching double digits for the second consecutive night.

St. Lucie fell to 7-14 in the second half and 40-47 overall with the loss. Palm Beach improved to 13-9 in the second half and 65-42 overall. The teams will decide the series Sunday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium with first pitch scheduled for 12:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Florida Falls Outside Top Five Most Retirement-Friendly States in New National Ranking
cards.teaser: Florida failed to secure a position among the top five most retirement-friendly states in a new national ranking released Sunday, challenging the state's long-held reputation as a
cards.body:
Florida failed to secure a position among the top five most retirement-friendly states in a new national ranking released Sunday, challenging the state's long-held reputation as a premier retirement destination. The assessment from Moneywise evaluated states based on factors affecting retirees' quality of life and financial security. The ranking represents a shift in how retirement destinations are evaluated across the United States, excluding a state that has traditionally dominated conversations about ideal places to spend retirement years.

Florida has traditionally marketed itself as an ideal location for retirees, with its warm climate and lack of state income tax serving as major draws for older Americans. The state's senior population has grown substantially over decades, with retirees from northeastern and midwestern states relocating to Florida communities in significant numbers. However, the new analysis considered multiple factors that affect retirement living, including cost of living, healthcare access, tax structures, and overall quality of life indicators. The exclusion of Florida from the top five suggests that other locations now offer more attractive combinations of affordability and amenities for retirees.

Florida has faced rising property insurance costs, increased housing prices, and higher overall living expenses in recent years, factors that may have influenced its position in the ranking. These economic pressures have created new challenges for retirees on fixed incomes who must balance the appeal of warm weather and outdoor lifestyles against escalating costs of maintaining their standard of living. Despite these financial headwinds, the findings arrive as Florida continues to see substantial population growth, with many new residents arriving at or near retirement age. The state's economy remains heavily dependent on retiree spending and the industries that support senior populations, including healthcare, real estate, and leisure services.

How this ranking affects future retirement migration patterns to Florida remains uncertain, though the state's established retirement communities and infrastructure continue to attract older Americans seeking warmer climates and outdoor lifestyles. The ranking signals that retirees now have compelling alternatives to consider when choosing their retirement destinations, potentially reshaping demographic trends that have favored Florida for generations. While the specific states that ranked in the top five were not detailed in the available information, Florida's absence from the list marks a notable development for a state whose identity and economy have been closely tied to its status as a retirement haven.

hero.headline: Florida Falls Outside Top Five Most Retirement-Friendly States in New National Ranking
hero.teaser: Florida failed to secure a position among the top five most retirement-friendly states in a new national ranking released Sunday, challenging the state's long-held reputation as a
hero.body:
Florida failed to secure a position among the top five most retirement-friendly states in a new national ranking released Sunday, challenging the state's long-held reputation as a premier retirement destination. The assessment from Moneywise evaluated states based on factors affecting retirees' quality of life and financial security. The ranking represents a shift in how retirement destinations are evaluated across the United States, excluding a state that has traditionally dominated conversations about ideal places to spend retirement years.

Florida has traditionally marketed itself as an ideal location for retirees, with its warm climate and lack of state income tax serving as major draws for older Americans. The state's senior population has grown substantially over decades, with retirees from northeastern and midwestern states relocating to Florida communities in significant numbers. However, the new analysis considered multiple factors that affect retirement living, including cost of living, healthcare access, tax structures, and overall quality of life indicators. The exclusion of Florida from the top five suggests that other locations now offer more attractive combinations of affordability and amenities for retirees.

Florida has faced rising property insurance costs, increased housing prices, and higher overall living expenses in recent years, factors that may have influenced its position in the ranking. These economic pressures have created new challenges for retirees on fixed incomes who must balance the appeal of warm weather and outdoor lifestyles against escalating costs of maintaining their standard of living. Despite these financial headwinds, the findings arrive as Florida continues to see substantial population growth, with many new residents arriving at or near retirement age. The state's economy remains heavily dependent on retiree spending and the industries that support senior populations, including healthcare, real estate, and leisure services.

How this ranking affects future retirement migration patterns to Florida remains uncertain, though the state's established retirement communities and infrastructure continue to attract older Americans seeking warmer climates and outdoor lifestyles. The ranking signals that retirees now have compelling alternatives to consider when choosing their retirement destinations, potentially reshaping demographic trends that have favored Florida for generations. While the specific states that ranked in the top five were not detailed in the available information, Florida's absence from the list marks a notable development for a state whose identity and economy have been closely tied to its status as a retirement haven.

hero.headline: JetBlue ending Vero Beach to New York JFK route in September due to low demand
hero.teaser: JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as th
hero.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating in September. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast. Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said the decision reflects how the airline industry operates based on passenger numbers. "It's just the way that that market works, and air carriers will fluctuate based off of demand," Dambeck said. He added that JetBlue "just wasn't seeing what they were hoping for" with the New York route.

Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot at success. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time if given more opportunity. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. He noted the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach, saying, "It's easy. It's close." His comments reflect concerns from local travelers who appreciated having direct access to New York without driving to larger airports in South Florida or Orlando.

The Boston route continues to perform well at Vero Beach Regional Airport, with Dambeck saying "Boston is seeing great demand." Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time, demonstrating continued interest in that northeastern connection. The contrast between the two routes highlights how different markets can perform differently even when serving similar geographic regions. While both Boston and New York are major northeastern cities, the Boston service has attracted enough passengers to remain viable while the JFK route struggled to build a sustainable customer base.

Dambeck said the door is not closed on the JFK route returning in the future, noting "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back." This leaves open the possibility that JetBlue could restore service to New York if conditions change or demand increases. Airlines regularly reassess their route networks based on seasonal patterns, economic conditions, and shifting travel preferences. For now, Vero Beach travelers seeking to reach New York will need to connect through other cities or use alternative airports.
